title: Optimize layer reuse and hybrid build-cache PoC to cut CI latency and image bloat
creator: Avery Lin
description: Legacy CI images and a high rate of cache misses are inflating build times and spend. This ticket scopes and implements a proof-of-concept to (1) reduce Docker layer duplication across service images, (2) introduce a hybrid build-cache strategy (local BuildKit cache + S3-backed remote CAS + selective priming), and (3) standardize lint/toolchain delivery via stable toolchain images. Goal: cut median CI build wall time for critical pipelines by ~40% and reduce cache miss rate below 10% for nightly and PR runs.
acceptance_criteria: PoC demonstrates 30-50% median build time reduction on three representative services (runtime, api-gateway, console) compared to baseline
Remote cache hit-rate >= 90% for warm workflows; measurable priming reduces cold-starts by >= 60%
Average CI image size reduced by >= 20% for targeted images through layer deduplication and modular base layers
Lint/toolchain removal from ad-hoc install scripts and moved to versioned toolchain images with automated upgrades in a single PR
Changes land behind a feature flag and can be rolled back with a single CI config flip
Documentation and runbook for operations and troubleshooting added to Confluence
work_items: Audit top-50 CI Dockerfiles for duplicated layers and large payloads (node_modules, apt caches, transient toolchains)
Design modular base image family: base-os, runtime-libs, language-runtimes, dev-tools (small, versioned)
Prototype BuildKit local + S3 remote cache integration and a cache-priming job
Benchmark three representative pipelines and capture tokenized timeline traces
Refactor lint/toolchain installation to rely on toolchain images and publish upgrade policy
Add metrics (cache hits/misses, upload latency, image size) to CI dashboards and alert on regressions
notes: Spike done: built a minimal BuildKit + s3 cache prototype; encountered multipart upload throttling on large artifacts (see comment)
We will scope the first rollout to non-blocking nightly jobs and one PR pipeline for runtime services to reduce blast radius
Estimate includes engineering + 1 day of security review + 2 days of ops runbook writing
